title: One output-phase step
statement: Let $x$ be a Boolean word, and let $c$ be a four-tape interpreter configuration on input $x$. Let $b$ be a Boolean word, $q$ a timed-interpreter control, $q'$ an optional timed-interpreter control, $p\in\mathbb{Z}$ a buffer-head position, $o$ a Boolean output word, $d\in\{-1,0,1\}$ a head movement, and $e$ an optional Boolean. Suppose that for every input symbol and every tuple of work-tape symbols, whenever lane $5$ contains at its head the symbol stored in $c$'s output buffer at position $p$, the transition from $q$ is an administrative action that leaves the clock lane unchanged, moves the buffer lane by $d$, emits $e$, and enters control $q'$. Then one step from the lifted configuration in control $q$, with buffer head at $p$ and real output $o$, yields the lifted configuration in control $q'$, with buffer head at $p+d$ and real output $o$ followed by $e$, if present.
hypotheses_covered: $c$ is a four-tape interpreter configuration on input $x$
For every input and work-tape read, if lane 5 reads the output-buffer content of $c$ at position $p$, the transition is the specified timed administrative action
replaced:
Suppose that, whenever the output-buffer lane reads its designated symbol, the
timed interpreter's transition in control $q$ is a pure buffer move by
$d \in \{-1,0,1\}$ with an optional real emission.  Then one step from the
output-phase configuration moves only the buffer head by $d$, appends the
optional emission to the real output, and passes to the designated control.
